# At a glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Format | Standard (Reality Fracture, set code `fra`, plus Standard mana and support) |
| Colors | Black, blue, green (Sultai) |
| Archetype | Surveil-reanimation built on the prepared mechanic |
| Size | 60 cards, 24 lands, 36 spells and creatures |
| Primary win | Grave Researcher reanimates a creature every upkeep for free, then the creatures it brings back attack: Proft (5/5 menace for three), Lasyd Prowler (5/5) and Vampire Soulcaller (flying 3/2) |
| Secondary win | Fblthp, Impossibly Lost: the deck mills itself so hard that drawing from an empty library during combat ends the game |
| Land as engine | Restless Reef is a 4/4 deathtouch attacker for four mana that mills four cards every time it attacks |

# Overview

Reality Fracture's prepared creatures are spells wearing a body. **Grave Researcher** is the cheapest engine in the set:
at the beginning of every upkeep it surveils 1, and if there are three or more creature cards in your graveyard it
becomes prepared. While prepared, you may cast a copy of its back face, **Reanimate** — a `{B}` sorcery that puts any
creature card from any graveyard onto the battlefield. Casting it unprepares the Researcher, and the next upkeep begins
the loop again.

That is the whole deck: fill the bin, turn the Researcher on, and reanimate every turn for one black mana. The fill is
cheap and repeatable — **Void Extrapolator** enters prepared and hands you a free **Omit Variables** (mill three),
**Patient Naturalist** mills three and returns a land, **Lasyd Prowler** mills for each land you control, and
**Restless Reef** mills four every time it attacks. By turn four the graveyard is a resource, not a loss.

The reanimation targets are chosen for what they do after they arrive. **Vampire Soulcaller** comes back and returns
another creature card from the graveyard to hand, so one Reanimate becomes two threats. **Proft, Sinister Mastermind**
is a 5/5 with menace for three mana, but only castable at threshold — which is exactly where this deck lives.
**Null Summoner** exiles a card from the opponent's hand on entry and, at threshold, lets you cast it with mana of any
type. **Winter, Tormented Loner** makes each opponent sacrifice a creature and grows with every creature card in your
graveyard.

Nothing here needs a specific pair to function. Every surveil makes the next reanimation better, and every creature in
the bin is another option for the Researcher.

# Approach

## Game plan phases

| Phase | Turns | What you are doing |
|---|---|---|
| Seed | 1–2 | Void Extrapolator prepared into a free mill three, or Servant of the Stinger to hold the ground. Patient Naturalist on two if the hand has no mill |
| Load | 3–4 | Grave Researcher plus a second mill source. The goal is three creature cards in the bin by the upkeep after the Researcher lands |
| Convert | 4–6 | Free Reanimate each upkeep. Bring back Proft for a 5/5, Soulcaller for a flier and a rebuy, or Winter for an edict |
| Close | 6+ | Restless Reef attacks and mills, Defossilize reanimates with two explores, Fblthp draws toward an empty library |

## Card roles

| Role | Cards | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prepared engine | Grave Researcher | 4 | Surveils every upkeep; becomes prepared at three or more creature cards in the graveyard, then casts Reanimate for free |
| Free mill | Void Extrapolator, Lasyd Prowler, Patient Naturalist | 9 | Extrapolator enters prepared for a free mill three; Prowler mills for each land; Naturalist mills three and rebuys a land |
| Reanimation | Defossilize, Reanimate (back face) | 2 plus engine | Defossilize is the hard cast; the Researcher's Reanimate is the repeatable one |
| Threshold payoffs | Proft, Null Summoner | 6 | Proft is a 5/5 menace for three at seven cards in the bin; Null Summoner exiles from hand and later casts the exiled card |
| Attrition | Winter, Hour of Defeat, Servant of the Stinger | 9 | Edict, destroy plus surveil, deathtouch blocker that commits crimes |
| Card flow | Vampire Soulcaller, Fblthp | 6 | Soulcaller rebuys a creature on entry; Fblthp draws two whenever an opponent is dealt combat damage |
| Manland | Restless Reef | 3 | 4/4 deathtouch for four, mills four on attack |

## Lands as engines

| Land | Copies | What it does for the deck |
|---|---|---|
| Restless Reef | 3 | Becomes a 4/4 deathtouch Shark; every attack mills four cards, which is a reanimation target and a threshold enabler |
| Underground Mortuary | 2 | Black-green source that surveils on entry |
| Blooming Marsh, Botanical Sanctum | 6 | Untapped on turns one and two, which is where this deck needs its mana |
| Overgrown Tomb, Breeding Pool | 4 | Untapped duals for two life; the life is affordable because the deck does not race |
| Opulent Palace | 2 | The only three-colour source; keep hands that need it only if another blue or green land is present |

## Curve and mana

Twenty-four lands, sixteen of them green sources and twelve blue, with fifteen black. The curve tops out at five:

| Cost | Count | Cards |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 9 | Void Extrapolator, Fblthp, Servant of the Stinger |
| 3 | 14 | Grave Researcher, Winter, Proft, Patient Naturalist |
| 4 | 5 | Null Summoner, Hour of Defeat |
| 5 | 8 | Vampire Soulcaller, Defossilize, Lasyd Prowler |

The opening hand wants two lands and a mill effect. Double-black is the only real constraint (Proft, Null Summoner,
Defossilize); the deck never needs double green before turn four, when Lasyd Prowler asks for it.

# Gameplay strategy

## Early game

Lead with the cheapest mill. Void Extrapolator on turn two, cast the free Omit Variables, and the bin already has three
cards. Servant of the Stinger is the other cheap early play: a 1/3 deathtouch that blocks everything relevant and
commits a crime whenever it is aimed at an opponent, which turns on its own tutor trigger for a card.

Do not trade the Researcher for a blocker. It is the engine; it survives behind a deathtouch body or a Winter edict.

## Mid game and the combo turn

The combo turn is any upkeep from turn four onward:

1. Upkeep: Grave Researcher surveils 1. If the surveilled card is a creature, the bin count rises; if not, it goes to
   the graveyard anyway as a threshold card.
2. If there are three or more creature cards in the graveyard, the Researcher becomes prepared.
3. Cast the copy of Reanimate for `{B}`. Choose the best creature in any graveyard.
4. The Researcher is unprepared and the board has a new threat. Next upkeep, repeat.

Sequencing matters: cast sorcery-speed mill (Patient Naturalist, Lasyd Prowler) before the upkeep trigger resolves when
you can, and hold the free Reanimate for the turn you can also attack with the returned creature.

## Win condition two

Fblthp, Impossibly Lost is a two-mana 1/1 that draws two cards whenever an opponent is dealt combat damage, and wins
the game outright if your library is empty at that moment. Between Restless Reef, Patient Naturalist, Lasyd Prowler and
a surveil every upkeep, the library empties in long games. Fblthp shuffles itself back in, so the deck never decks
itself out of a win: it is a second, independent axis that costs two slots.

## Mulligan guide

| Hand | Keep? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Two lands, Void Extrapolator, any three-drop | Keep | Mill on two, engine on three |
| One land, no one-drop | Mulligan | The deck needs two mana by turn two to function |
| Three lands, Grave Researcher, Patient Naturalist, Winter | Keep | Engine plus two mill sources |
| All five-drops and lands | Mulligan | No way to load the bin before turn five |
| Opulent Palace as the only coloured source | Mulligan | Three-colour tapland with nothing to do on one |

## Key interactions

- **Threshold is a switch, not a bonus.** Proft cannot be cast with six cards in the graveyard. Surveil and mill are
  how the deck turns it on; do not exile your own graveyard for value.
- **Reanimate is not restricted to your graveyard.** Against a deck that has already traded creatures, the Researcher
  can take their best creature. That is often better than anything in your own bin.
- **Void Extrapolator's threshold bonus** makes it a 3/3 at seven cards, and its free Omit Variables is a mill three
  every time a fresh copy enters prepared.
- **Winter wants a sacrifice.** Cast it with a body you do not need, or with a creature that already attacked.

## Matchups

| Opponent | Plan |
|---|---|
| Aggro | Trade early with Servant of the Stinger and Hour of Defeat, then reanimate their best attacker. Winter's edict is the stabiliser |
| Control | Do not overextend into a sweeper; the Researcher engine rebuilds from the graveyard, so keep one threat in hand |
| Ramp | Race with Proft and Lasyd Prowler, and use Null Summoner to strip their payoff from hand before threshold turns it into your card |
| Graveyard hate | The deck still attacks with a 5/5 for three and a 4/4 manland; side out one copy of Defossilize first |

# Iterations

| Round | Change | Metrics |
|---|---|---|
| v1 | Self-mill grind shell: Marwyn, Ferocity of the Hunt, Extended Absence, Blessed Ghoul, Theoretical Necromancer around the surveil core | sim 24.0%, synergy 70.9, T4 0.557, P4L 0.565 — FAIL on sim |
| v2 | -Marwyn, -Ferocity of the Hunt, -Extended Absence, -Blessed Ghoul; +Grave Researcher x4, +Void Extrapolator x4, +Null Summoner x3, +Souls of the Lost x4, +Cruel Somnophage x3 | sim 4.0%, synergy 70.2, T4 0.639, P4L 0.631 — FAIL on sim |
| v3 | -Souls of the Lost, -Cruel Somnophage, -Tarmogoyf; +Servant of the Stinger x3, +Vampire Soulcaller x4, +Patient Naturalist x3, +Hour of Defeat x2, +Defossilize x2, +Fblthp x2 | sim 57.0%, synergy 70.4, T4 0.637, P4L 0.642 — PASS |

v1 to v2: the reanimation engine arrived but the variable-power bodies (power `*`) were read as zero-power creatures by
the simulator, so the deck had no clock. v2 to v3: fixed-stat creatures that do something on entry replaced them, and
the win rate moved from 4 to 57 percent.
